newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - March 13.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on the front page of its business section on Thursday:

WASHINGTON - After two all-night negotiating sessions, Staples Inc. struck a deal to sell 63 stores to its rival Office-Max for $109 million, which company executives and industry experts said should clear the way for Staples to merge with Office Depot.

WASHINGTON - In an economy where prices are routinely given in pennies, nickels, dimes and dollars, the stock market's practice of quoting prices in eighths of a dollar has seemed a puzzling oddity to many investors.

WASHINGTON - The former accountant for a Northern Virginia technology company pleaded guilty to fraud charges in Las Vegas and simultaneously settled a civil stock fraud case brought by the Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington.
WASHINGTON - The D.C. Economic Development Corporation proposed by President Clinton could revive dozens of distressed neighborhoods, business and community leaders said.
